raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On the Rust server, non-streamed requests with a named or `required` `tool_choice` return no `tool_calls` when the parser is `pythonic`, `glm47`, `minimax-m3` or `gemma4`. The calls stay in `content` as a JSON array, with finish reason `stop`.

This affects `SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1` (off by default) deployments running GLM-4.7-Flash with its cookbook flags or `pythonic`, which `docs/docs/advanced_features/tool_parser.mdx` documents for Llama-3.2-1B and the Llama 4 cookbook recommends for tool calling.

On main, 0 of 40 Llama-3.2-1B `pythonic` requests and 0 of 3 GLM-4.7-Flash requests returned calls per choice. With this diff, 40 of 40 and 3 of 3 did, with finish reason `tool_calls` and no `content`. Rust streaming and the Python server with `pythonic` return `tool_calls`.

With no structural tag, `tool_constraint` gives these choices a JSON schema, and the non-streaming path passes that JSON only to the parser, which does not read it.

Neither #47622 (Python server, no parser) nor draft #46521 (Rust API migration) fixes this path, but #46521 conflicts in `chat.rs` and `tools.rs` on a trial merge.

## Modifications

When that schema applies, the non-streaming path reads the bare JSON first, as Dynamo's streaming jail does. If this finds no call, the tool-call parser runs as on main. Other requests do not change.

`llama3` and `mistral` already read bare JSON. On a server, I found one change: a forced string argument with `<|python_tag|>` or `[TOOL_CALLS]` now returns calls.

## Accuracy Tests

```text
setup:      Rust server on one B200, 63c6de2eda with and without this diff (its rust/ tree matches 99fd01047d)
prompt:     Call sub with int_a=7 and int_b=2. Do not call get_weather.
named tool: get_weather (search in the forced string rows)
sampling:   temperature 0.8, top_p 0.8, one seed per request
max tokens: 200 on Llama-3.2-1B (400 in the forced string rows), 2048 on GLM-4.7-Flash and Qwen3-4B
```

| Model, parser, choice | Mode | Requests with calls, main | Requests with calls, this diff |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Llama-3.2-1B, `pythonic`, named and required | Non-streamed | 0 of 40 each | 40 of 40 each |
| Llama-3.2-1B, `pythonic`, named and required | Streamed | 40 of 40 each | 40 of 40 each |
| Llama-3.2-1B, `glm47`, `minimax-m3`, `gemma4`, named and required (parsing path only, because the schema decides the output shape) | Non-streamed | 0 of 3 each | 3 of 3 each |
| Llama-3.2-1B, `llama3`, named, plain and strict tools | Non-streamed | 40 of 40 each | 40 of 40 each |
| Llama-3.2-1B, `llama3`, named | Streamed | 40 of 40 | 40 of 40 |
| Llama-3.2-1B, `mistral`, named and required (parsing path only) | Non-streamed | 3 of 3 each | 3 of 3 each |
| Llama-3.2-1B, `llama3`, `mistral`, named and required, schema enum forces a string with the markers, `parallel_tool_calls=false` | Non-streamed | 0 of 3 each | 3 of 3 each, exact arguments |
| Llama-3.2-1B, `llama3`, `mistral`, same string, named | Streamed | 3 of 3 each | 3 of 3 each |
| GLM-4.7-Flash, `--attention-backend triton --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45` (cookbook flags), named and required | Non-streamed | 0 of 3 each | 3 of 3 each |
| Qwen3-4B, `--tool-call-parser pythonic --reasoning-parser qwen3` (the cookbook parser is `qwen25`), named and required | Non-streamed | 0 of 3 each | 3 of 3 each |
| GLM-4.7-Flash and Qwen3-4B, same flags, named and required | Streamed | 3 of 3 each | 3 of 3 each |

No named request in these rows returned another tool.

The new test fails on the Rust class on main with `No tool_calls: '[{"name": "get_tourist_attractions", ...` and passes with this diff. `test_openai_function_calling.py` found no regression on a B200. `pre-commit` on a merge with `99fd01047d` found no issue in the changed files, with clippy on Linux.

As on main, output cut by max tokens with `[f(a=1)]` or `<tool_call>` in a string can return another tool on `pythonic` and `glm47`.

Not run: MiniMax-M3 weights, Llama 4, AMD, NPU, more than one GPU, and runtime CI. `unsloth/gemma-4-E2B-it` does not start (`no Rust MM pipeline for model_type='gemma4'`).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. This adds one JSON parse to these non-streamed requests.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

files.patch:
@@ -906,6 +906,38 @@ def test_pythonic_tool_call_prompt(self):
             f"Function name '{names}' should container either 'get_weather' or 'get_tourist_attractions'",
         )
 
+    def test_pythonic_forced_tool_choice(self):
+        """
+        Test: A named or required tool_choice constrains the output to a JSON array
+        that the pythonic parser does not read, and a non-streaming response still
+        returns it as tool_calls.
+        """
+        client = openai.Client(api_key=self.api_key, base_url=self.base_url)
+        for tool_choice, allowed_names in (
+            (
+                {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_tourist_attractions"}},
+                {"get_tourist_attractions"},
+            ),
+            ("required", {"get_weather", "get_tourist_attractions"}),
+        ):
+            response = client.chat.completions.create(
+                model=self.model,
+                messages=self.PYTHONIC_MESSAGES,
+                tools=self.PYTHONIC_TOOLS,
+                tool_choice=tool_choice,
+                temperature=0.1,
+                max_tokens=2048,
+                stream=False,
+            )
+            choice = response.choices[0]
+            self.assertTrue(
+                choice.message.tool_calls, f"No tool_calls: {choice.message.content!r}"
+            )
+            self.assertEqual(choice.finish_reason, "tool_calls")
+            for tool_call in choice.message.tool_calls:
+                self.assertIn(tool_call.function.name, allowed_names)
+                json.loads(tool_call.function.arguments)
+
     def test_pythonic_tool_call_streaming(self):
         """
         Test: Streaming pythonic tool call format; assert tool_call index is present.
